explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge with human evaluation by reporting Cohen's kappa agreement scores between GPT-4o and native speakers across the same evaluation metrics (GM, GA, Q) applied to the same summaries generated with and without guardrails.

prompts.notes: Paper includes verbatim prompts for GM, GA, and Q in Appendix E. Evaluation uses both Individual assessments (single summary evaluated on all metrics) and Side-by-Side evaluations comparing guardrail vs baseline summaries.

guidelines.notes: Human evaluations used same GM, GA, Q metrics as LLM evaluators. Human annotators were native speakers with linguistics training (76%) following detailed annotation practices described in Section 8.

sample_size.notes: Evaluations done on 20 gold transcripts per language (subsampled 27 languages for human evaluation). Validation uses same instances evaluated by both humans and LLMs.

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Not explicitly stated, but kappa values indicate varying agreement levels

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM judgments show moderate agreement with humans on GA (κ=0.42) but poor alignment on GM (κ=0.14) and Q (κ=0.03); LLMs particularly struggle with low-resource languages and show position bias in SBS evaluation for quality.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluators used identical criteria (Binary GM/GA, Ternary Quality) on the same set of summaries, enabling direct validation.
